title: Inferring Urban Mobility Interactions from Aggregated Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2609.07349v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Real-time urban governance depends not only on knowing where people are, but on how they move between places, directional flows that could be conventionally resolved by tracking individuals through space, i.e., expensive to sustain and built on traces that are highly unique and readily re-identifiable. Here we show that this directional structure need not be observed to be known: aggregated counts which cities already collect retain enough information to reconstruct the temporal evolution of origin-destination (OD) matrix. Using an uncertainty-aware physics-informed framework, we infer future OD flows from area-level counts alone across twelve mobility datasets from cities in the United States and China, reaching accuracy comparable to models that take historical OD matrices as input. translated_title: 从聚合动态中推断城市出行交互
translated_abstract: 实时城市治理不仅需要知道人们在哪里，还需要了解人们如何在地点之间移动——这种方向性流动传统上需要通过在空间中追踪个体来解析，这种方式维护成本高昂，且建立在高度独特、极易被重新识别的轨迹数据之上。本研究表明，这种方向性结构无需被直接观测即可获知：城市已经在收集的聚合计数数据保留了足够的信息，可用于重建出发地-目的地（OD）矩阵的时间演化。利用一个具有不确定性感知的物理信息框架，我们仅从区域级别的计数数据中推断未来的OD流量，并在来自美国和中国城市的十二个出行数据集上进行了验证，其准确性可与以历史OD矩阵为输入的模型相媲美。概率建模纠正了对稀疏、高价值通道的系统性低估，并产生了与观测数据相符的校准预测。
tldr: 仅利用城市已有的聚合区域计数数据，通过不确定性感知的物理信息框架即可准确推断未来的出发地-目的地流量，无需追踪个体轨迹，在保护隐私的同时达到与依赖历史OD矩阵的模型相当的精度。
en_tdlr: Aggregated area-level counts alone are sufficient to accurately reconstruct future origin-destination flows through an uncertainty-aware physics-informed framework, achieving accuracy comparable to models using historical OD matrices while avoiding privacy-invasive individual tracking.
